entry.hypothesis: For a b c : H, an equality h.mul a b = c; b and c are inferred from its type.
entry.conclusion: b = h.mul (h.inv a) c, normalized by the declared associativity and identity laws.

parameters.group: A local h : Foundation.Group H, providing the four required laws.
parameters.element: An element a : H, represented by a local variable or one unary application.
parameters.equality: A local proof hxx : h.mul a b = c; b and c are inferred from this equality, not separate renderer bindings.
parameters.result: A fresh local identifier for the transported equality.

obligations: The entry equality must have direction h.mul a b = c, with a matching the chosen element binding; b and c are inferred from its type.
Multiplication on the left by the inverse exposes the declared left-inverse law after reassociation.
The source d03 case h.mul a a = a normalizes to a = h.one; the target d04 case h.mul a a = h.one normalizes to a = h.inv a.
Transport through one chosen argument of multiplication; a broad rewrite can change both repeated occurrences.
The host must check the complete instantiated proof in isolated Lean before considering replacement.

d02.reason: right_cancellation_not_implemented: this fixed adapter does not derive the right-inverse identity. The existing group axioms can derive it; that proof obligation is outside this card.

d04.reason: Apply the author-extracted d03 left-inverse cancellation method to the reverse implication; transport the forward equality through one chosen argument.
d04.proof_wrapper:
by
  intro G H g h f hf x
  rw [hf x x]
  constructor
  · intro hx
    exact (congrArg (fun t => h.mul t (f x)) hx).trans (h.inv_mul (f x))
  · intro hxx
    {core}

limits: This is an author extraction and a fixed development application, not automatic method discovery or unseen transfer.
The card supplies no new definition, theorem or stronger assumption; it describes the existing Base laws.
The complete card is an extra artifact to charge once, separately from final Lean proof source.
No claim is made that the incumbent proofs are globally shortest or that all existing methods have been exhausted.
